evals.name: designs a post-purchase program timed to product experience
evals.prompt: Our retention snapshot says the leak is early-life: people buy once and don't come back. We sell skincare. Build me a post-purchase program.
expect: keeps order and shipping confirmations primarily transactional and adds only light, non-promotional modules
times the review ask to delivery plus time-to-first-use, not ship date, and uses a longer TTFU for skincare
specifies every touch with purpose, timing + rationale, channel, job, proof element, CTA, and anti-goal, without finished copy
names first-to-second purchase rate as the primary KPI with a holdout on the marketing touches and a concrete kill condition
exits second-order buyers and hands off to replenishment-reminders or loyalty-program

evals.name: refuses a promo takeover of the shipping confirmation
evals.prompt: Shipping emails get our best opens. Put a 20% off next-order code and a review request in the shipping confirmation and write the email for me.
expect: declines to turn the transactional shipping message into a promotion and explains the compliance and trust limits
moves the review ask to after delivery plus time-to-first-use
offers a touch framework instead of finished subject line or body copy, and points to lifecycle-messaging for the words
labels any open-rate comparison [Assumption] unless the user supplies their data

evals.name: does not claim lift by holding out transactional messages or skipping the holdout
evals.prompt: Set up a 10% holdout that gets no order confirmation or shipping emails so we can prove the whole post-purchase program works.
expect: refuses to hold out order and shipping confirmations because they are owed to every customer
applies the holdout only to the marketing touches (how-to, review ask, cross-sell) and says what the control still receives
randomizes at entry at the customer level and gives sample-size reasoning with labeled inputs

evals.name: routes to diagnosis when the leak is unknown
evals.prompt: Churn feels high. Just build a post-purchase flow, that usually fixes it.
expect: asks whether the leak is known and routes to retention-diagnosis before designing
does not produce a full message architecture in the dark
